label: prop:closure-unseen-subword
title: No closure distinguishes two elements exactly when they differ by a commutator; closure is a Bell pairing
html:
Let R be a commutative ring and A an R-algebra. Call an R-linear map t : A \to M a trace if t(xy) = t(yx) for all x, y \in A, and let [A, A] be the R-span of all xy - yx.

  1. For a, b \in A, every trace satisfies t(a) = t(b) if and only if a - b \in [A, A]. The quotient map A \to A/[A, A] = \mathrm{HH}_0(A) is the universal trace.

  2. For a unit u \in A and any w \in A, every trace satisfies t(u w u^{-1}) = t(w).

  3. Let \Omega = \sum_i e_i \otimes e_i \in R^n \otimes R^n. For every X \in M_n(R),

      (X \otimes 1)\,\Omega = (1 \otimes X^{\mathsf T})\,\Omega,
  \qquad
  \langle \Omega, (X \otimes 1)\,\Omega \rangle = \mathrm{tr}\,X .

Proof. (1) A trace vanishes on each generator xy - yx of [A, A], so by linearity it vanishes on [A, A]; this gives the reverse direction. The quotient map A \to A/[A, A] is itself a trace, because xy - yx \in [A, A]. Applying the hypothesis to it gives a - b \in [A, A]. (2) u w u^{-1} - w = (uw)u^{-1} - u^{-1}(uw) is a commutator, so (1) applies. (3) Both sides of the first identity have (i, j) entry X_{ij}, and \langle \Omega, (X \otimes 1)\Omega \rangle = \sum_i X_{ii}. \square

In the braid setting, A = H_n(q) and the closure of a braid word is a trace on A (Markov trace). Item (1) says what a closure cannot see. The relation a \sim b \iff a - b \in [A, A] is exactly the fibre of the map to Hochschild homology \mathrm{HH}_0. Item (3) is the form closure takes on a matrix algebra: the coevaluation prepares \Omega, the evaluation projects onto it.
